messages:
morgan: heads-up — started rolling gpu-base:2026.02 with nvidia-container-toolkit 1.14 in eu-west-1. ~3% of gpu pods failing to start, complaining about libcuda/libnvidia-ml not found. filing here before we widen the rollout.

ravi: can you paste one failing pod / describe and logs?

morgan: sure — here's one example: 
```
$ kubectl describe pod gpu-trainer-7f8b9 -n prod
State:          Waiting
Reason:         CrashLoopBackOff
Init Containers: 0
Containers:
  trainer:
    Image:  our-registry/gpu-trainer:stable
    Mounts:
      /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 from host-nvidia (ro)
Events:
  Warning  FailedMount  10s (x3 over 30s)  kubelet, ip-10-0-1-45  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "host-nvidia": mount failed: exit status 32
    mount error: no such file or directory
```

And container logs show runtime error from libcudart: 
```
/usr/local/bin/entrypoint: error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

jen: this smells like the toolkit's mount shim changed behavior around user namespaces / mount propagation in 1.14. we saw earlier that 1.14 switches to a bind-propagation mode that doesn't expose host files into containers running with userns-remap. any of these nodes using userns or custom runtimeclass?

oscar: not intentionally. these are Dedicated GPU nodes using driver 515 on the host. rollout was supposed to be purely the userland toolkit in the image. suspect mismatch: toolkit 1.14 might be expecting a newer driver (>=525) or different symlink layout for libnvidia-ml.

ravi: do we have a quick repro on a node? can we run `docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint ls` to check host mount visibility?

morgan: repro on node ip-10-0-1-45 attached: 
```
# on node
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so*
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 17 Jan  8  2026 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> libnvidia-ml.so.515.76
# inside a container started by kubelet with toolkit 1.14
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ | grep libcuda
ls: cannot access '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1': No such file or directory
```

jen: workaround for now: pin toolkit to 1.13.x in the gpu-base image and redeploy, or add an explicit hostPath volume mount to the pod spec to force lib paths in. both suck but will buy time. also open a ticket with NVIDIA for a regression.

oscar: +1 rollback. I'll prepare an image build with toolkit=1.13.3 and trigger a limited rollback in eu-west-1 only. we should also cordon older nodes while we verify.

morgan: created changelist to pin and started a canary in the eu-west-1 staging pool. early result: canary pods come up fine. reverting the rollout for prod.

deploy-bot: Started deployment rollback for deployment/gpu-trainer to image gpu-base:2026.01-toolkit1.13.3 (by oscar) — 2/3 replicas updated. :gear:

ravi: we should also capture the mount error + audit logs and attach to NVIDIA ticket. /var/log/messages on the node should have `nvidia-container-toolkit` mount calls.

morgan: copied /var/log/syslog and kubelet logs, filed ticket #NVIDIA-REG-3421 with attachments and the node kernel/driver versions: kernel 5.15.0-102, nvidia-driver 515.76.05, toolkit 1.14.0. ticket says investigation queued.

sre-robot: incident created: INC-2026-0345 — "nvidia-toolkit 1.14 mount regression in eu-west-1". severity: P2. Assigned: eng-platform + eng-infra. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-0345

jen: follow-ups: 1) publish a note on infra-runbook about pinning toolkit vs driver compatibility matrix, 2) add a preflight check in node image pipeline to verify expected host lib paths before rolling toolkit, 3) add a canary gate that checks a simple cuda hello-world pod after toolkit image change.

morgan: agreed. for now rollback completed, prod pods back to green. will update the incident with RCA once NVIDIA responds. :white_check_mark:
